_description: Species-specific fracture profiles for synthetic fragment generation. Each species defines fracture type probabilities and edge roughness parameters. Edit these to tune realism per species.

_fracture_types.root_loss: Break at or near the root-crown junction, losing the root/base
_fracture_types.tip_loss: Break losing the apex/tip of the crown
_fracture_types.lateral_break: Diagonal/oblique break removing one side of the tooth
_fracture_types.edge_chip: Chip along the blade edge or serration margin
_fracture_types.diagonal_snap: Oblique fracture across the crown at an angle
_fracture_types.transverse_snap: Vertical/near-vertical break across the tooth, exposing wide dentine cross-section
_fracture_types.oblique_front: Steep angled fracture biased toward the labial face, exposing prominent dentine

_edge_params.roughness: Overall jaggedness of fracture edge (0.0=smooth, 1.0=very jagged)
_edge_params.curvature: How much the fracture follows the tooth's natural curvature (0.0=straight, 1.0=follows contour)
_edge_params.edge_3d_width: Width in pixels of the 3D cross-section effect at the fracture edge
_edge_params.dentine_color_mode: 'auto' (sample darker tooth area + lighten) or 'manual' (use dentine_color_min/max)
_edge_params.dentine_clarity_pct: Auto mode: % to lighten from the darker tooth surface (0=same as dark side, 100=white)
_edge_params.dentine_color_min: Manual mode: [R,G,B] minimum of the dentine color range
_edge_params.dentine_color_max: Manual mode: [R,G,B] maximum of the dentine color range
_edge_params.dentine_edge_darken_pct: % to darken the dentine at the outer edge (0=same, 50=half brightness). Simulates mineralized fossil edge.

Otodus Megalodon._notes: Large triangular teeth. Thick enameloid produces angular, conchoidal fractures. Root-crown junction is the primary weak point. Bourlette area is vulnerable. Thick cross-section means transverse/oblique breaks expose prominent dentine.

Carcharodon Carcharias._notes: Similar to megalodon but thinner crown. More prone to tip loss. Enameloid is thinner so fractures are sharper. Oblique front breaks expose thin but visible dentine layer.

Hemipristis Serra._notes: Distinctive curved blade with large serrations. Curved shape makes lateral breaks common. Transverse breaks across the curved blade expose wide dentine bands.

Galeocerdo Cuvier._notes: Cockscomb/notched shape. Distal notch is a stress concentrator. Wide flat crown means transverse breaks produce broad dentine exposure.

Carcharhinus Leucas._notes: Small narrow triangular teeth. Narrow tip is most fragile. Oblique front fractures on thin crown expose proportionally more dentine.

Negaprion Brevirostris._notes: Thin, narrow, smooth-edged teeth. No serrations so no edge chipping. Clean diagonal and transverse snaps are common. Thin cross-section limits dentine exposure.
